name: Corteva, Inc.
one_line_reason: What trades as CTVA since 1 October 2026 is only the crop-protection half of old Corteva (seed was spun off as Vylor), and it fell 24% on 12 November after a Brazil-driven cut to its first standalone guidance; the screen's 50% FCF yield is a spin-off artifact, but the real business still looks cheap.
evidence: Seed was distributed as Vylor (VYLR) on 1 Oct 2026 (8-K filed 2026-10-05), so the FY2025 figures in the screen (revenue $17.4B, FCF $2.8B) mostly belong to another company. Q3 2026 pro forma net sales fell 9% to $1.59B with Latin America organic -31% (volume -24% on channel stock and farmer credit stress, price -7% on generic pressure on late-life molecules) while North America was +7%, EMEA +14% and Asia +5%; FY2026 operating EBITDA guide cut to $1.10-1.125B from about $1.3B (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-12). Crop protection segment EBITDA ran $1.07B (2019), $1.00B (2020), $1.68B (2022 peak), $1.35B (2025) per the 10-Ks, so 2026 is a return to the 2019-20 floor, not a collapse; pro forma 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet shows $1.8B cash against $1.0B debt and $0.8B pension.
key_numbers: Price $8.36 (2026-11-18), mcap $5.6B; EV ~$4.8B = ~4.4x 2026 guided EBITDA $1.1B; P/E ~10.7x guided operating EPS $0.76-0.80; P/B ~0.47 (pro forma equity $11.9B); screen FCF yield 50% is an artifact

name: CF Industries Holdings, Inc.
one_line_reason: CF looks cheap only on earnings swollen by a 2026 nitrogen supply shock (the Gulf conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure lifted urea prices), and the stock has already risen 43% in a year to reflect it; a low multiple on peak-cycle profit is normal, not a mispricing.
evidence: Q3 2026 results (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-04): LTM adjusted EBITDA $3.8B and LTM net earnings $2.2B versus FY2025 net income of $1.80B and a 2016-2020 range of $0.4-0.9B, with 97% ammonia capacity utilization and Yazoo City still offline until 1H 2027. LTM free cash flow was $2.0B (53% of EBITDA, held down by a $306M deposit to Canada in a transfer-pricing dispute), and $1.3B went back to shareholders. Revenue history shows the cycle plainly: $11.2B in 2022, $5.9B in 2024, then up again; news coverage (used only as a lead) ties the 2026 spike to a 77% urea price jump after the Hormuz closure.
key_numbers: Price $113.70 (2026-11-18), +43% 1y, -18% from 3y high; P/E ~7.5x LTM ($2.2B) and 9.3x FY2025; EV/LTM adj. EBITDA ~4.5x; 10y median P/E 10.9x; shares -25% in 5y

name: Celanese Corporation
one_line_reason: Celanese is a leveraged chemical company still paying for its 2022 debt-funded purchase of DuPont's Mobility & Materials unit at the top of the cycle; the business underneath is recovering (beat-and-raise in Q3 2026), but the equity is a thin slice on top of roughly $10B of net debt.
evidence: Q3 2026 release (8-K filed 2026-11-02): net sales +6% to $2.56B, operating EBITDA $548M (21% margin) vs $517M a year earlier, free cash flow $461M; full-year adjusted EPS guided to $6.00-6.25 and FCF raised to $750-800M, with net debt to operating EBITDA expected near 4.7x at year end. The 2024-25 GAAP losses came from a $1.1B Engineered Materials goodwill impairment and other write-downs (EDGAR shows $5.8B of impairments over 3 years), and the dividend was cut to a token level in 2025 (dividends paid $0.31B in 2024 vs $0.01B in 2025). Management targets about $1B of divestiture proceeds by end-2027 (about $650M by end-2026, including Micromax and a further 19% of Nutrinova for $152M).
key_numbers: Price $48.21 (2026-11-18), -71% from 3y high, +33% 1y; P/E ~7.9x 2026 adj. EPS guide (on an 8% adjusted tax rate); FCF yield ~14.6% on guide; net debt ~$10.2B, ~4.7x EBITDA; EV ~$15.5B ~7x EBITDA

name: The Trade Desk, Inc.
one_line_reason: The Trade Desk's revenue has stopped growing and is now guided to shrink about 11% because Amazon's cut-price ad-buying platform and agency fee fights are eroding both its share and its take rate; a former 20%+ grower losing pricing power is a broken moat, not a dip.
evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $736M, -0.5% y/y (vs +18% in Q3 2025), net income $38M vs $116M, adjusted EBITDA margin 36% vs 43% (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-09). Q4 2026 guidance of at least $755M compares with about $851M in Q4 2025 (FY2025 $2.90B less 9M 2025 $2.049B), a decline of roughly 11%. Stock-based pay of $0.49B a year eats most of the $0.78B FY2025 free cash flow. CEO Jeff Green bought 6.0M shares for $148M at $23.49-25.08 on 2-4 March 2026 (Form 4s); the stock is now $15.52.
